_comment: The ports map (ANDROID_PORT.md §13.3). One entry per Kotlin file, each
naming the FULL set of Swift sources it ports and the sha each was ported
from. Kotlin files are many-to-one against Swift: AttestationService is
five files, ConfidentialSession four, ProviderStore three.
The checker walks this map and runs `git log <sha>..HEAD -- <path>`
against a teemoon-ios checkout. It MUST assert each path still exists at
HEAD and hard-error otherwise: on a renamed or deleted file git log
returns empty, which reads as 'no drift', and this repo renames and
Ported TEST files belong here too (rule 4). teemoon-ios encodes every new
invariant as a test first, so a test-only commit is a behavior change no
REBUILD rows point at a contract doc, not a Swift file — the transcript,
Keychain, HTTPTransport, LiteRTTransport and BackgroundWork have no Swift

acceptedDivergences.why: a DEBUG launch-argument route that boots the real app into one styled screen, because Xcode Previews render without the composition root and under-style the capture. Paparazzi has no such gap — it renders through TeemoonTheme with the real primitives — so the Android form of this is the snapshot suites (DesignSnapshotTest, TrustScreenSnapshotTest, ModelBrowserSnapshotTest, PlacesKeysSnapshotTest, the two WhereSheet ones), the same reasoning that waives ChatView+Previews.swift. The launch-extra half that IS needed on a device — seeding a screen into a known state — is UiTestSeeding's extras.

two token groups. `ML` — only `ML.accent` (#FF7A1A) is used anywhere in the Swift, by WhereChip, Appearance and WhereSheetView+FirstRun, and Theme.kt already carries it with the rationale (the product orange, NOT systemOrange). `ML.bg/ink/muted/faint/hair` and the whole of `Timing` are referenced by nothing in the iOS tree — verified 2026-09-21, an orphan of an onboarding flow that no longer exists (Views/Onboarding/ holds this file and nothing else). Porting them would import dead constants and invite someone to build to them.

namedAssetExists asks the asset catalogue whether a vendor logo exists, so a provider tile can draw one instead of a monogram. MEASURED 2026-09-21: it can never answer yes on iOS either. The tile looks up `provider-logo-<name>` and the catalogue ships `logo-brave`, `logo-grok`, `logo-fireworks`, `logo-nearai` — the names do not match, nothing else in the Swift references those four assets, and ProviderIdentityTile is the function's only caller. So BOTH platforms render the monogram, and Android reaches that by not asking a question whose answer is always no. Kotlin's equivalent is Resources.getIdentifier, which is discouraged, defeats resource shrinking, and would be dead here. Reported to the iOS session as a bug on their side (four shipped assets nothing can show, one branch nothing can reach) — if they fix the names, this becomes a port and a real visual difference.
acceptedDivergences.revisitWhen: iOS fixes the asset names, or Android ships vendor logos of its own.

acceptedDivergences.why: a one-method protocol so attestation, key check and search validation can run against planted bytes. OkHttp's client is already that seam and is already used as one: EndpointDirectory, LMStudioAdapter, OllamaAdapter, ProviderKeyValidation and EndpointModelCatalog all take `client: OkHttpClient` with a lazy default, and the tests pass a MockWebServer-backed one. A Kotlin `interface HttpClient` wrapping it would be a second seam over the first, and the ports map would then have to say which one a call site is allowed to use.

UIApplication.beginBackgroundTask brackets, so a request in flight survives the user leaving the app. Android has no per-task equivalent and needs none at this scale: a coroutine keeps running when the activity stops, and the process is only killed under memory pressure. What Android DOES need for the long case — a model download surviving the app — is WorkManager, which is an open product decision (a new notification surface and a dependency-allowlist question) and not this file.
acceptedDivergences.revisitWhen: the WorkManager download decision is made; this is the iOS half of it.

acceptedDivergences.why: hides iOS 26's automatic scroll-edge effect, because SwiftUI would otherwise attach one to the transcript's collection view and fight the app's own viewport-fixed overlays. Compose draws no edge effect to hide; the overlays themselves are ChatFadeBand and GlassEdge in ChatScreen.kt, which are mapped. There is nothing left to turn off.

samples the streaming reply on a CADisplayLink so Textual re-layouts run at the frame rate instead of once per token. Compose's recomposition is ALREADY frame-clocked: state written between frames coalesces into one recomposition on the next MonotonicFrameClock tick, which is the same sampling this class hand-builds. Adding a pacer on top would add a frame of latency and nothing else. The half that is NOT free — not re-rendering settled blocks — is MarkdownStreamSplitter.kt, which is mapped. NOTE the measured lesson in the Swift, which applies here: the first version capped at 15-24 fps and that ceiling, not the markdown renderer, was what made streaming look chunky (p95 87ms between updates). Do not reintroduce a throttle on the transcript tail.

thirteen lines: `typealias ProvidersSettingsView = PlacesKeysHubView`, kept so older Swift navigation and tests that name the old type still compile. Nothing in Kotlin names it — PlacesKeysHubScreen is reached by callback, not by type name — so the alias would have no referent and no compile to keep working.

networkDestinations._comment: §4 of the port spec is the complete list of hosts this app may talk to. Adding one is a PRODUCT decision, not an implementation detail (CONTRIBUTING.md). openrouter.ai and integrate.api.nvidia.com were approved by the user on 2026-09-20 for the 1.0.2 batch; every other addition needs the same answer. build.nvidia.com added 2026-09-21 as part of the approved NVIDIA preset: it is a LINK TARGET (KnownModel.modelPageURL), not an API the app calls, and every other vendor's equivalent is already here — docs.near.ai, console.x.ai, app.fireworks.ai, huggingface.co. The gate surfaced it rather than letting it slip, which is the point; it is recorded here rather than waived.
